answer_summary:
An MCP server, most commonly referring to a **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server**, acts as a crucial bridge between Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, particularly large language models (LLMs), and external tools or data sources, including Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). This protocol standardizes the communication, allowing AI agents to access real-time data, perform actions, and utilize specialized features not inherent in their training data.

In the context of paid API calls, an MCP server facilitates the interaction of AI models with these monetized external services. While the MCP server itself doesn't typically handle the billing, it enables the AI to make requests to APIs that may operate under various monetization models.
